The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has said that Jigawa needs a listening leader, not a furious one. Lamido made the remarks while speaking during a series of strategic stakeholders’ meetings held across the state’s three senatorial districts ahead of the 2027 general elections. The meetings, which involved stakeholders from Jigawa South-West, North-East and North-West Senatorial Districts, were aimed at commencing preparations for the 2027 election campaign. Speaking at the Gumel meeting held on Sunday, which was the third and final leg of the strategic stakeholders’ meetings across the three senatorial districts, the PDP governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections, Mustapha Sule Lamido, said the state was in dire need of a compassionate and listening leader. Lamido stated that Jigawa did not need a leader who was always angry and furious with his people, but one who listened, understood their pains, and responded to their needs and aspirations. He noted that only a leader who carried every part of the state along, without sectionalism, and who prioritised the welfare of the people could bring the desired development and prosperity to Jigawa. Lamido said Jigawa did not need a sectional leader who looked after only a particular region. “Jigawa today does not need a leader who is sectional or who looks after only a particular region, but one who puts Jigawa first in its entirety to ensure development in all ramifications,” he said. Lamido alleged that there had been a decline in education, health, and many other sectors under the current leadership in the state. “In my view, the style of this present government does not befit our people,” he said in Hausa. He assured the people that a vote for the PDP was a trust that would bring benefits to the voter. “Whoever gives the PDP his vote, it is as if he has given it as amana, and he will enjoy the benefit of the vote he gave. “If you elect us, we promise that, Insha Allah, we will help you and do for you what will make you happy,” he assured. He added that the party needed unwavering commitment from its supporters to the progress, development and prosperity of the state during the forthcoming elections. According to him, “We also deliberated on several important issues and discussed strategic plans towards achieving our collective goals in 2027.” He, however, recalled how discussions with key stakeholders proceeded during the North-East Senatorial District meeting, held in Hadejia, where leaders from 85 wards attended. Lamido said the target remained the progress, development and prosperity of the beloved state. “This is the third and final leg of the strategic meetings that we are holding today (Sunday) in Gumel, the headquarters of Jigawa North-West Senatorial District,” he declared. He thanked the party’s supporters and well-wishers and urged them to remain committed and united ahead of the elections. Lamido also promised old members of the PDP who had remained loyal since the party lost power 12 years ago. He therefore urged them to exercise more patience, saying that the party was with them and that they would soon rejoice if God granted it victory in the forthcoming elections. In his address at the meeting, the Jigawa State Chairman of the PDP, Babandi Ibrahim Gumel, said the party was fully prepared and ready for the 2027 polls. He commended Mustapha Sule Lamido for the strategic meetings and said the massive turnout across the three senatorial districts showed the level of acceptance of the party. Gumel said the party would continue to engage stakeholders from all wards across the state to ensure victory in 2027. Salisu Kabuga
